utterance: The account already publishes the public domain `example53.com` from its primary Route 53 hosted zone. The service reached at `service.example53.com` now runs in two places: 192.0.2.101 in us-east-1 and 192.0.2.102 in eu-central-1. Using Route 53 resources, configure a routing policy on that name which navigates users to the least congested endpoint — one A record per region, TTL 60, each with its own set identifier.

main.responsibility: owns the application's resources and their configuration
main.intent: in the pre-existing example53.com hosted zone, service.example53.com is answered by a latency-routed set of two non-alias A members with distinct set identifiers — one bound to us-east-1 answering 192.0.2.101 and one bound to eu-central-1 answering 192.0.2.102 — each with a 60-second TTL, so a caller is sent to whichever endpoint is quickest to reach from it
